title.zh: 卷一百八十四 列傳第七十一: 王都中 王克敬 任速哥 陳思謙 韓元善 崔敬
title.en: Volume 184 Biographies 71: Wang Douzhong, Wang Kejing, Ren Suge, Chen Siqian, Han Yuanshan, Cui Jing
title.raw: 卷一百八十四 列傳第七十一: 王都中 王克敬 任速哥 陳思謙 韓元善 崔敬 Volume 184 Biographies 71: Wang Douzhong, Wang Kejing, Ren Suge, Chen Siqian, Han Yuanshan, Cui Jing

sentences.zh: 王都中

translations.literal: Wang Douzhong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Douzhong

sentences.zh: 王都中，字元俞，福之福寧州人。

translations.literal: Wang Douzhong, styled Yuanyu, was a man of Funing Prefecture in Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Douzhong, styled Yuanyu, was a native of Funing Prefecture in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 父積翁，仕宋為寶章閣學士、福建制置使。

translations.literal: His father Jiweng served the Song as Baozhang Pavilion Academician and Fujian Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiweng had served the Song as Academician of the Baozhang Pavilion and Commissioner for Pacification of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，宋主納土，乃以全閩八郡圖籍來，入覲世祖於上京，降金虎符，授中奉大夫、刑部尚書、福建道宣慰使，兼提刑按察使，尋除參知政事，行省江西。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, when the Song ruler surrendered territory, he brought the registers of all eight prefectures of Min, went to the Upper Capital to pay homage to Shizu, surrendered the golden tiger tally, and was appointed Central Submitter Grand Master, Minister of Punishments, Pacification Commissioner of the Fujian Circuit, concurrently Investigating Censor, then removed as Vice Administrator, acting Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276, when the Song sovereign submitted his realm, Jiweng brought the registers of all eight prefectures of Fujian, went to the Upper Capital to pay homage to Kublai Khan, surrendered his golden tiger tally, and received appointment as Central Submitter Grand Master, Minister of Punishments, Pacification Commissioner of the Fujian Circuit, and concurrent Investigating Censor; shortly afterward he was made Vice Administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄以為國信使，宣諭日本，至其境，遇害於海上。

translations.literal: Soon he was made credentialed envoy to announce and instruct Japan; when he reached its borders he met with harm on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed credentialed envoy to Japan, but was killed at sea when he reached Japanese waters.

sentences.zh: 都中生三歲，即以恩授從仕郎、南劍路順昌縣尹。

translations.literal: Douzhong at age three was by grace appointed Attendant Gentleman and magistrate of Shunchang County in Nanjian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong was only three when, by grace of the throne, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and magistrate of Shunchang County in Nanjian Circuit.

sentences.zh: 七歲，從其母葉訴闕下，世祖閔焉，給驛券，俾南還，賜平江田八千畝、宅一區。

translations.literal: At seven, following his mother Ye he appealed at the palace gates; Shizu pitied them, gave travel warrants, and had them return south, granting eight thousand mu of fields in Pingjiang and one residence.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of seven he accompanied his mother Ye to appeal at court; Kublai Khan took pity on them, issued travel warrants for their return south, and granted them eight thousand mu of land in Pingjiang and a residence.

sentences.zh: 已而世祖追念其父功不置，特授都中少中大夫、平江路總管府治中，時年甫十七。

translations.literal: Thereafter Shizu, recalling his father's merit without cease, specially appointed Douzhong Junior Central Grand Master and Assistant Administrator of the Pingjiang Circuit General Administration, when he was only seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kublai Khan, ever mindful of his father's service, specially appointed Douzhong Junior Central Grandee and Assistant Administrator of the Pingjiang Circuit General Administration when he was only seventeen.

sentences.zh: 僚吏見其年少，頗易視之。

translations.literal: The staff officials, seeing him young, rather treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officials, seeing how young he was, tended to take him lightly.

sentences.zh: 都中遇事剖析，動中肯綮，皆咢眙不敢欺。

translations.literal: Douzhong, when matters arose, analyzed them; his judgments always hit the vital point, and all stared in astonishment and dared not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a matter arose, Douzhong analyzed it to the quick, always striking the heart of the issue, until his colleagues could only stare in astonishment and dared not try to deceive him.

sentences.zh: 崑山有詭易官田者，事覺，而八年不決，都中為披故牘，洞見底里，其人乃伏辜。

translations.literal: In Kunshan someone had fraudulently exchanged official fields; the matter was exposed yet eight years went without decision; Douzhong opened the old documents, saw through to the bottom, and the man then submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Kunshan a man had fraudulently exchanged official land; though the case came to light, it remained unresolved for eight years until Douzhong examined the old records, saw straight through to the truth, and the culprit finally submitted to punishment.

sentences.zh: 吳江有違拒有司築堤護田之令而歸過於眾人者，都中詢知其故，皆置不問，其人乃無所逃罪。

translations.literal: In Wujiang some who had defied the authorities' order to build dikes to protect fields shifted blame onto the crowd; Douzhong inquired and knew the reason, set all aside without questioning them, and the man then had nowhere to escape guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In Wujiang men who had defied the government's order to build dikes to protect their fields tried to shift blame onto the community at large; Douzhong investigated, learned the truth, and declined to pursue the others—whereupon the ringleader had no way to escape his guilt.

sentences.zh: 學舍久壞不治，而郡守缺，都中曰：「聖人之道，人所共由，何獨守得為乎？」

translations.literal: The schoolhouse had long been ruined and not repaired, while the prefect was absent; Douzhong said, "The Way of the sages is what all men may follow together—why should only the prefect be able to act?"
translations.idiomatic: The schoolhouse had long lain in ruins, and the prefect's post was vacant; Douzhong said, "The Way of the sages is a path for everyone—why should restoring it be the prefect's task alone?"

sentences.zh: 乃首募大家，合錢新其禮殿。

translations.literal: He then took the lead in soliciting great families, pooled money, and rebuilt its ritual hall.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the lead in soliciting contributions from leading families, pooled their funds, and rebuilt the ritual hall.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，除浙東道宣慰副使。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Zhedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 金華有毆殺人者，吏受賕，以為病死。

translations.literal: In Jinhua someone had beaten a man to death; the clerk took a bribe and reported it as death from illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinhua a man had been beaten to death, but the clerk took a bribe and reported the victim had died of illness.

sentences.zh: 都中摘屬吏覆按，得其情。

translations.literal: Douzhong selected subordinate clerks to reinvestigate and obtained the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong assigned subordinate clerks to reinvestigate the case and uncovered the truth.

sentences.zh: 獄具，縣長吏而下，皆以贓敗。

translations.literal: When the case was complete, from the county chief clerk downward all fell through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was closed, every official from the county magistrate down was ruined by bribery charges.

sentences.zh: 餘姚有豪民張甲，居海濱，為不法，擅制一方，吏無敢涉其境。

translations.literal: In Yuyao there was a powerful man Zhang Jia, dwelling on the seacoast, acting unlawfully and controlling a whole region alone; no clerk dared enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuyao a powerful local magnate named Zhang Jia lived on the coast, breaking the law and ruling his own stretch of territory so absolutely that no official dared set foot there.

sentences.zh: 都中捕系之，痛繩以法。

translations.literal: Douzhong arrested and detained him, and rigorously bound him by law.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong had him arrested and punished him to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 遷荊湖北道宣慰副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 適歲昆，都中躬履山谷，以拯其飢，民賴以全活者數十萬。

translations.literal: Just then the year was a Kun year [famine year]; Douzhong personally walked through valleys and hills to relieve their hunger, and the people who relied on him to survive whole numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought severe famine; Douzhong went in person through valleys and hills to relieve the starving, and several hundred thousand people owed their survival to him.

sentences.zh: 武宗詔更鈔法，行銅錢，以都中為通才，除江淮泉貨監。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong ordered the paper-note law changed and copper cash circulated; regarding Douzhong as broadly talented, he was appointed Supervisor of Currency for the Jianghuai region.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong ordered reforms to the paper-note system and the circulation of copper cash; deeming Douzhong a man of wide talent, the court appointed him Supervisor of Currency for the Jianghuai region.

sentences.zh: 凡天下為監者六，惟江淮所鑄錢號最精。

translations.literal: Of all the supervisors throughout the realm there were six, but only the coins cast by Jianghuai were finest in quality.
translations.idiomatic: There were six such mint supervisors throughout the empire, but only the coins cast under Jianghuai supervision were of the finest quality.

sentences.zh: 改郴州路總管。

translations.literal: He was changed to General Administrator of Chenzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as General Administrator of Chenzhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 郴居楚上流，溪洞徭獠往來民間，憚其強猾，莫敢與相貿易。

translations.literal: Chen lay in the upper reaches of Chu; Yao and Liao from stream grottoes and cave settlements came and went among the people; they feared their fierceness and craft, and none dared trade with them.
translations.idiomatic: Chenzhou lay in the upper reaches of the Chu region, where Yao and Liao tribesmen from the hill country moved among the populace; the people feared their fierceness and cunning and dared not trade with them.

sentences.zh: 都中煦之以恩，懾之以威，乃皆悅服。

translations.literal: Douzhong warmed them with kindness and awed them with authority, and then all came to delight in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong treated them with kindness and restrained them with authority, until they all submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 郴民染於蠻俗，喜鬥爭，都中乃大治學舍，作籩豆簠簋、笙磬琴瑟之屬，使其民識先王禮樂之器，延宿儒教學其中，以義理開曉之，俗為之變。

translations.literal: The people of Chen were steeped in barbarian custom and fond of fighting; Douzhong then greatly repaired the schoolhouse, made vessels such as platters, beans, grain containers, sheng pipes, chime-stones, zithers, and lutes, had the people recognize the ritual and music instruments of the former kings, invited old Confucians to teach therein, and enlightened them with moral principle, and custom thereby changed.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chenzhou had been steeped in frontier custom and were prone to brawling; Douzhong therefore renovated the schoolhouse on a large scale, commissioned ritual vessels and musical instruments of the ancient kind, and had the people learn to recognize the implements of the sages' rites and music; he invited veteran Confucian scholars to teach there and enlightened the people with moral principle, and local custom was transformed.

sentences.zh: 鄰州茶陵富民覃乙死，無子，惟一小妻，及其贅婿，妻誣其婿拜屍成婚，藏隱玉杯夜明珠，株連八百餘人，奉使宣撫移其獄，諉之都中，窮治，悉得其情，而正其罪。

translations.literal: In the neighboring prefecture Chaling, the wealthy man Qin Yi died without sons, having only a young wife and her uxorilocal son-in-law; the wife falsely accused the son-in-law of bowing before the corpse to complete marriage, concealed a jade cup and night-luminous pearl, and implicated more than eight hundred people; the imperial commissioner for pacification transferred the case and referred it to Douzhong, who exhaustively investigated, obtained all the facts, and rectified the crimes.
translations.idiomatic: In neighboring Chaling a wealthy man named Qin Yi died childless, leaving only a young wife and her uxorilocal son-in-law; the wife falsely accused the son-in-law of marrying over the corpse, concealed a jade cup and a night-luminous pearl, and implicated more than eight hundred people; when an imperial pacification commissioner transferred the case to Douzhong, he investigated to the end, uncovered the full truth, and secured proper convictions.

sentences.zh: 州長吏而下，計其贓至十一萬五千餘緡，人以為神明。

translations.literal: From the prefectural chief clerk downward, the bribes totaled more than 115,000 strings of cash, and people regarded him as divine in insight.
translations.idiomatic: From the prefectural chief clerk downward, the bribes uncovered amounted to more than 115,000 strings of cash, and the people regarded him as uncannily perceptive.

sentences.zh: 遷饒州路總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Administrator of Raozhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Administrator of Raozhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 年飢，米價翔踴，都中以官倉之米，定其價為三等，言於行省，以為須糶以下等價，民乃可得食，未報。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, rice prices soared; Douzhong took the grain from the official granary, fixed its price in three grades, and told the Branch Secretariat that it was necessary to sell at the lowest grade so the people could obtain food; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year rice prices soared; Douzhong took grain from the government granary, set three price grades, and reported to the Branch Secretariat that grain must be sold at the lowest grade if the people were to eat—but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 又於下等價減十之二，使民就糴。

translations.literal: He further reduced the lowest grade price by two-tenths and had the people come to buy grain.
translations.idiomatic: He then cut the lowest grade price by a further twenty percent and opened the granary for the people to buy grain.

sentences.zh: 時宰怒其專擅，都中曰：「饒去杭幾二千里，比議定往還，非半月不可。

translations.literal: The chief minister was angry at his usurpation of authority; Douzhong said, "Raozhou is nearly two thousand li from Hangzhou; by the time deliberation is settled and the journey made back and forth, no less than half a month is required.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister was furious at his unauthorized action; Douzhong replied, "Raozhou is nearly two thousand li from Hangzhou; by the time a decision is made and word travels back and forth, half a month will have passed.

sentences.zh: 人七日不食則死，安能忍死以待乎！」

translations.literal: A man who goes seven days without eating dies—how can they endure death while waiting!"
translations.idiomatic: A man who goes seven days without food dies—how can the starving be expected to wait for death while we deliberate!"

sentences.zh: 其民亦相與言曰：「公為我輩減米價，公果得罪，我輩當鬻妻子以代公償。」

translations.literal: The people also said to one another, "The lord reduced the rice price for us; if the lord truly incurs guilt, we shall sell wives and children to repay on his behalf."
translations.idiomatic: The people among themselves said, "Our lord lowered the price of rice for us; if he is truly punished, we will sell our wives and children to pay his fine for him."

sentences.zh: 時宰聞之乃罷。

translations.literal: When the chief minister heard this he then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief minister heard this, he dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 郡歲貢金，而金戶貧富不常，都中考得其實，乃更定之。

translations.literal: The commandery annually presented gold tribute, but the wealth of gold households was not constant; Douzhong investigated and obtained the facts, then revised the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture paid an annual gold tribute, but the wealth of gold-mining households fluctuated; Douzhong investigated the true circumstances and revised the assessments.

sentences.zh: 包銀之法，戶不過二兩，而州縣征之加十倍，都中責之，一以詔書從事。

translations.literal: Under the wrapped-silver law no household owed more than two taels, yet prefectures and counties levied ten times that; Douzhong held them accountable and had all proceed according to the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Under the wrapped-silver levy no household owed more than two taels, yet prefectures and counties were collecting ten times that amount; Douzhong held them to account and enforced the edict as written.

sentences.zh: 父老或以兩岐之麥、六穗之禾為獻，都中曰：「此聖主之嘉瑞，非臣下所敢當。」

translations.literal: The elders sometimes presented wheat with double ears or grain with six stalks; Douzhong said, "These are auspicious omens of the sage ruler—not what a subject dares to accept."
translations.idiomatic: Local elders once presented wheat with double ears and grain with six stalks to a single head; Douzhong said, "These are auspicious omens belonging to the sage ruler—they are not for a subject such as myself to accept."

sentences.zh: 遂以聞於朝。

translations.literal: He then reported them to the court.
translations.idiomatic: He forwarded them to the court instead.

sentences.zh: 以內憂去郡，民生為立祠。

translations.literal: He left the commandery on account of domestic mourning, and the people in his lifetime erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: When he left the prefecture on account of domestic mourning, the people erected a shrine to him in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除兩浙都轉運鹽使，未上，擢海北海南道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was appointed Director of Salt Transport for the Two Zhe circuits, but before he took office was promoted to Purifying Censor of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed Director of Salt Transport for the Two Zhe circuits, but before he could take up the post he was promoted to Purifying Censor of the Haibei and Hainan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 中書省臣奏國計莫重於鹽策。

translations.literal: A member of the Central Secretariat memorialized that in state finance nothing was heavier than the salt policy.
translations.idiomatic: A Central Secretariat official memorialized that nothing weighed more heavily on state finance than the salt policy.

sentences.zh: 乃如前除鹽亭灶戶，三年一比附推排，世祖舊制也。

translations.literal: It was then as before to remove salt-pavilion stove households, with triennial comparison and reassessment—an old institution of Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly the old practice was restored of reassessing salt-pavilion and stove households every three years—an institution established by Kublai Khan.

sentences.zh: 任事者恐斂怨，久不舉行。

translations.literal: Those in charge feared gathering resentment and for a long time did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Officials in charge had long feared provoking resentment and had not carried it out.

sentences.zh: 都中曰：「為臣子者，使皆避謫，何以集事？」

translations.literal: Douzhong said, "As subjects, if all avoid blame, how may affairs be brought together?"
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong said, "If every official shunned blame, how would anything ever get done?"

sentences.zh: 乃請於行省，遍曆三十四場，驗其物力高下以損益之。

translations.literal: He then requested of the Branch Secretariat to go through all thirty-four fields, verify the high and low of their material resources, and increase or decrease accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the Branch Secretariat for permission to visit all thirty-four salt fields, assess each household's means, and adjust levies accordingly.

sentences.zh: 役既平而課亦足，公私便之。

translations.literal: When corvée labor was settled and the levy also sufficient, public and private alike were benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Corvée burdens were eased, revenues were met, and both government and people benefited.

sentences.zh: 擢福建閩海道肅政廉訪使，俄遷福建道宣慰使都元帥，又改浙東道宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Purifying Censor of the Fujian Minhai Circuit, soon transferred to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Fujian Circuit, then changed to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Zhedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Purifying Censor of the Fujian Minhai Circuit, soon afterward made Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of Fujian, and then transferred to the same posts in the Zhedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，被省檄，整點七路軍馬，境內晏然。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianli reign he received a Branch Secretariat order to muster troops of the seven circuits, and within the borders all was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianli reign he was ordered by the Branch Secretariat to muster troops across seven circuits, and the region remained entirely tranquil.

sentences.zh: 徙廣東道宣慰使都元帥，三易鎮，皆佩元降金虎符。

translations.literal: He was moved to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of the Guangdong Circuit; three times he changed garrison posts, each time wearing the golden tiger tally bestowed by the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Pacification Commissioner and Commander-in-Chief of Guangdong; over three successive postings he wore the golden tiger tally bestowed by the Yuan court.

sentences.zh: 元統初，朝廷以兩淮鹽法久壞，詔命都中以正奉大夫、行戶部尚書、兩淮都轉運鹽使，仍賜襲衣法酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong, because the Liang-Huai salt law had long been ruined, the court ordered Douzhong as Regular Submitter Grand Master, Acting Minister of Revenue, and Director of Salt Transport for the Two Huai circuits, still granting court robes and ritual wine.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuantong reign, seeing that the Liang-Huai salt system had long been in disarray, the court appointed Douzhong Regular Submitter Grand Master, Acting Minister of Revenue, and Director of Salt Transport for the Two Huai circuits, and granted him court robes and ritual wine.

sentences.zh: 都中既至，參酌前所行於兩浙者，次第施行之，鹽法遂修。

translations.literal: Once Douzhong arrived, he weighed what had previously been carried out in the Two Zhe circuits and implemented it step by step; the salt law was thereby restored.
translations.idiomatic: Once Douzhong arrived, he adapted the reforms he had carried out in the Two Zhe circuits and applied them in sequence, and the salt system was restored.

sentences.zh: 尋拜河南行省參知政事，中道以疾作南歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, but on the way illness arose and he returned south.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, but fell ill en route and returned south.

sentences.zh: 於是天子閔其老，詔即其家拜江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Son of Heaven pitied his age and ordered that at his home he be appointed Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, taking pity on his age, then appointed him Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat at his own home.

sentences.zh: 至正元年卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Zhizheng reign (1341).

sentences.zh: 贈昭文館大學士，諡清獻。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, with posthumous title Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall, with the posthumous epithet Qingxian (Clear Offering).

sentences.zh: 都中歷仕四十餘年，所至政譽輒暴著，而治郡之績，雖古循吏無以尚之。

translations.literal: Douzhong served in office more than forty years; wherever he went his governmental reputation was suddenly prominent, and in governing commanderies his achievements—even ancient compassionate officials could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong served in office for more than forty years; wherever he went his reputation for governance was immediately conspicuous, and his achievements as a prefectural administrator would have done credit even to the compassionate officials of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 當世南人以政事之名聞天下，而位登省憲者，惟都中而已。

translations.literal: In his age southerners who were known throughout the realm for administrative affairs and yet reached provincial and censorial posts were only Douzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Among southerners of his day who won a national reputation for administrative talent and rose to provincial or censorial rank, Douzhong stood alone.

sentences.zh: 又其清白之操，得於家傳，所賜田宅之外，不增一疃，不易一椽，廩祿悉以給族姻之貧者，人尤以是多之。

translations.literal: Moreover his integrity in conduct came from family transmission; beyond the fields and residences granted him he did not add one plot or change one rafter, and his salary grain he entirely gave to poor clansmen and affines, and people especially for this praised him more.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity, inherited from his family tradition, was equally renowned: beyond the fields and residence granted by the throne he added not a single plot nor altered a single beam, and he gave his entire official salary to poor kinsmen and in-laws, for which people admired him all the more.

sentences.zh: 幼留京師，及拜許衡，即知所趨向。

translations.literal: In youth he remained in the capital; when he paid respects to Xu Heng he at once knew the direction to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his youth in the capital, and once he paid his respects to Xu Heng he knew at once the path he should follow.

sentences.zh: 中年尤致力於根本之學，自號曰本齋。

translations.literal: In middle age he especially devoted himself to fundamental learning and styled himself Benzhai (Root Studio).
translations.idiomatic: In middle age he devoted himself especially to fundamental learning and took the style Benzhai (Root Studio).

sentences.zh: 有詩集三卷。

translations.literal: He had a poetry collection in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a poetry collection in three juan.

sentences.zh: ○王克敬

translations.literal: ○ Wang Kejing
translations.idiomatic: ○ Wang Kejing

sentences.zh: 王克敬，字叔能，大寧人。

translations.literal: Wang Kejing, styled Shuneng, was a man of Daning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kejing, styled Shuneng, was a native of Daning.

sentences.zh: 幼奇穎，嘗戲道旁，丞相完澤見之，謂左右曰：「是兒資貌秀偉，異日必令器也。」

translations.literal: In youth he was extraordinarily clever; once playing by the roadside, Chancellor Wanze saw him and said to those at his side, "This boy's endowment and appearance are elegant and grand; another day he will surely be a fine vessel."
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright; once while playing by the roadside he was seen by Chancellor Wanze, who said to his attendants, "This boy is handsome and gifted; one day he will surely prove a man of consequence."

sentences.zh: 大寧朔土，習尚少文，而克敬獨孜孜為儒者事。

translations.literal: Daning was frontier soil; custom favored little learning, yet Kejing alone diligently pursued Confucian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Daning was frontier country, where learning was little valued, yet Kejing alone devoted himself diligently to Confucian studies.

sentences.zh: 既仕，累遷江浙行省照磨，尋升檢校。

translations.literal: Once in office he was repeatedly promoted to Registrar of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, then soon advanced to Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: After entering office he rose through successive appointments to Registrar and then Proofreader of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 徽州民汪俊上變，誣富人反，省臣遣克敬往驗之。

translations.literal: A Huizhou commoner Wang Jun submitted a memorial of sudden change, falsely accusing the wealthy of rebellion; the provincial officials sent Kejing to verify it.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner of Huizhou named Wang Jun submitted an urgent memorial falsely accusing wealthy men of rebellion; the provincial authorities sent Kejing to investigate.

sentences.zh: 克敬察其言不實，中道數為開陳禍福，俊悔，將對簿，竟仰藥以死。

translations.literal: Kejing perceived his words were not true; on the way he several times explained fortune and misfortune; Jun repented, and when about to face trial he finally took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing saw that the accusation was false and several times along the way explained to Jun the consequences he faced; Jun repented, and on the eve of trial took poison and died.

sentences.zh: 調奉議大夫、知順州，以內外艱不上。

translations.literal: He was transferred as Grand Master for Discussion and Prefect of Shunzhou, but on account of inner and outer mourning did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Grand Master for Discussion and Prefect of Shunzhou, but did not take up the post on account of mourning obligations.

sentences.zh: 除江浙行省左右司都事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Left and Right Bureaus of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延祐四年，往四明監倭人互市。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanyou he went to Siming to supervise the Japanese mutual-market trade.
translations.idiomatic: In 1317 he was sent to Siming to supervise trade with Japanese merchants.

sentences.zh: 先是，往監者懼外夷情叵測，必嚴兵自衛，如待大敵。

translations.literal: Before this, those who went to supervise feared the foreign barbarians' intentions were hard to fathom and always kept strict troops for self-defense, as if awaiting a great enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Previously supervisors had feared the unpredictability of foreign traders and always went heavily armed, as if facing a major enemy.

sentences.zh: 克敬至，悉去之，撫以恩意，皆帖然無敢嘩。

translations.literal: When Kejing arrived he removed them all, treated them with kind intent, and all were docile and none dared make uproar.
translations.idiomatic: When Kejing arrived he dismissed all such precautions, treated the traders with kindness, and they became entirely docile, none daring to cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 有吳人從軍徵日本陷於倭者，至是從至中國，訴於克敬，願還本鄉。

translations.literal: There was a man of Wu who followed the army in the campaign against Japan and was trapped among the Japanese; now he came with them to China, appealed to Kejing, and wished to return to his native district.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Wu who had been captured in Japan while serving in the campaign against that country now came to China with the traders, appealed to Kejing, and asked to return home.

sentences.zh: 或恐為禍階，克敬曰：「豈有軍士懷恩德來歸而不之納邪！

translations.literal: Some feared this would be a source of calamity; Kejing said, "How could there be a soldier who comes in gratitude and virtue and is not received!
translations.idiomatic: Some feared this might invite trouble; Kejing said, "How can we refuse a soldier who comes in good faith seeking to return home!

sentences.zh: 脫有釁，吾當坐。」

translations.literal: If trouble should arise, I shall bear the penalty."
translations.idiomatic: If trouble should arise from this, I alone will bear the blame."

sentences.zh: 事聞，朝廷嘉之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the court commended him.

sentences.zh: 番陽大饑，總管王都中出廩粟賑之，行省欲罪其擅發，克敬曰：「番陽距此千里，比待命，民且死，彼為仁，而吾屬顧為不仁乎！」

translations.literal: Poyang suffered great famine; the General Administrator Wang Douzhong released granary grain to relieve it; the Branch Secretariat wished to punish his unauthorized distribution; Kejing said, "Poyang is a thousand li from here; by the time orders arrive the people will be dead—he acted with benevolence, and should we attendants instead act without benevolence!"
translations.idiomatic: When Poyang suffered severe famine, Wang Douzhong released government grain to relieve the starving; the Branch Secretariat wished to punish him for unauthorized distribution; Kejing said, "Poyang is a thousand li away; by the time orders arrive the people will be dead—he acted humanely, and are we to be inhumane instead!"

sentences.zh: 都中因得免。

translations.literal: Douzhong thereby escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Douzhong was thereby spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，用故事監吏部選。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor and, following precedent, supervised the Ministry of Personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor and, following precedent, supervised the Ministry of Personnel's civil-service selection.

sentences.zh: 有履歷當升者，吏故抑之，問故，吏曰：「有過。」

translations.literal: Someone whose record qualified for promotion was deliberately held down by a clerk; asked the reason, the clerk said, "There was a fault."
translations.idiomatic: A candidate whose record qualified him for promotion was deliberately held back by a clerk; when Kejing asked why, the clerk said, "He has a disciplinary record."

sentences.zh: 克敬曰：「法，笞四十七以上不升，今不至是。」

translations.literal: Kejing said, "By law, forty-seven strokes of the cane or more bar promotion; now it does not reach that."
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "The law bars promotion only for offenses of forty-seven strokes of the cane or more; this does not reach that threshold."

sentences.zh: 吏曰：「責輕罪重。」

translations.literal: The clerk said, "The charge was light but the crime heavy."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk replied, "The formal charge was light, but the actual offense was serious."

sentences.zh: 曰：「失出在刑部，銓曹安知其罪重！」

translations.literal: He said, "Errors belong to the Ministry of Punishments—how should the selection bureau know the crime was heavy!"
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "Errors in sentencing belong to the Ministry of Punishments—how should the selection bureau know whether the offense was truly serious!"

sentences.zh: 卒升之。

translations.literal: In the end he promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted the man in the end.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史張伯高曰：「往者監選以減駁為能，今王御史乃論增品級，可為世道賀矣。」

translations.literal: The Secretariat Censor Zhang Bogao said, "In the past supervising selection took reduction and rejection as ability; now Censor Wang discusses raising grades—this may be congratulated for the age."
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Censor Zhang Bogao remarked, "In the past censors supervising selection prided themselves on blocking promotions; now Censor Wang argues for raising grades—this is something the age may celebrate."

sentences.zh: 尋遷左司都事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Left Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時英宗厲精圖治，丞相拜住請更前政不便者，會議中書堂，克敬首言：「江南包銀，民貧有不能輸者，有司以責之役戶，甚無謂也，當罷之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Yingzong vigorously sought good governance; Chancellor Bayiju requested revision of previous policies that were inconvenient; meeting in the Central Secretariat hall, Kejing was first to speak: "In Jiangnan wrapped silver—when the people are poor and cannot pay, the authorities shift blame to corvée households; this is very pointless and should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Yingzong was vigorously pursuing good governance; Chancellor Bayiju called for revision of inconvenient policies from the previous reign; at a meeting in the Central Secretariat hall Kejing spoke first: "In Jiangnan the wrapped-silver levy falls on the poor who cannot pay, and officials shift the burden to corvée households—this is absurd and should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 兩浙煎鹽戶牢盆之役，其重者尤害民，當免其它役。」

translations.literal: In the Two Zhe circuits the salt-boiling households' labor on the salt pans—where heavy it especially harms the people—should be exempted from other corvée."
translations.idiomatic: In the Two Zhe circuits the heaviest corvée burdens on salt-boiling households, especially work on the salt pans, are especially harmful and those households should be exempted from other corvée duties."

sentences.zh: 議定以聞，悉從之。

translations.literal: When deliberation was settled and reported, all were followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the proposals were reported to the throne, all were approved.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，出為紹興路總管，郡中計口受鹽，民困於誅求，乃上言乞減鹽五千引。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he went out as General Administrator of Shaoxing Circuit; in the commandery salt was allotted per capita and the people were distressed by exactions; he therefore memorialized requesting reduction of salt by five thousand yin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiding reign he was appointed General Administrator of Shaoxing Circuit, where salt was allotted per capita and the people were crushed by exactions; he memorialized requesting a reduction of five thousand yin of salt.

sentences.zh: 運司弗從，因歎曰：「使我為運使，當令越民少蘇矣。」

translations.literal: The transport office did not consent; he therefore sighed and said, "If I were transport commissioner, I could let the people of Yue breathe a little easier."
translations.idiomatic: The transport office refused; he sighed and said, "If I were transport commissioner, I could give the people of Yue some relief."

sentences.zh: 行省檄克敬抽分舶貨，拗蕃者例籍其貨，商人以風水為解，有司不聽。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat ordered Kejing to assess shares of incoming ship cargo; by precedent those who forced down prices on foreign goods registered their cargo; merchants pleaded wind and water as excuse, and the authorities would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat ordered Kejing to assess duties on incoming ship cargo; by precedent merchants who forced down prices on foreign goods had their entire cargo confiscated; when merchants pleaded that storms had driven them off course, the authorities would not listen.

sentences.zh: 克敬曰：「某貨出某國，地​​有遠近，貨有輕重，冒重險，出萬死，捨近而趨遠，棄重而取輕，豈人情邪！」

translations.literal: Kejing said, "Such goods come from such a country; distances have near and far, goods have heavy and light; braving heavy peril and escaping ten thousand deaths, abandoning the near to rush to the far, discarding the heavy to take the light—how is this human feeling!"
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "Each cargo comes from a particular country; distances vary and goods differ in value; to brave deadly perils, abandon nearby ports for distant ones, and leave valuable goods for lighter ones—how is that human nature!"

sentences.zh: 具以上聞，眾不能奪，商人德之。

translations.literal: He fully reported upward; the crowd could not overrule him, and merchants were grateful.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the full reasoning to the court; none could overturn his judgment, and the merchants were grateful.

sentences.zh: 擢江西道廉訪司副使，轉兩浙鹽運司使，首減紹興民食鹽五千引。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Censor of the Jiangxi Circuit, transferred to Commissioner of the Two Zhe Salt Transport Office, and first reduced Shaoxing people's salt consumption by five thousand yin.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Censor of the Jiangxi Circuit and then appointed Commissioner of the Two Zhe Salt Transport Office, where his first act was to reduce Shaoxing's salt allotment by five thousand yin.

sentences.zh: 溫州逮犯私鹽者，以一婦人至，怒曰：「豈有逮婦人千百里外，與吏卒雜處者，污教甚矣！

translations.literal: In Wenzhou when arresting violators of private salt they brought one woman; he angrily said, "How can there be arresting a woman a thousand li away to mix with clerks and soldiers—this greatly stains instruction!
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzhou arrested private-salt offenders and brought a woman prisoner a thousand li away to be confined among clerks and soldiers, he said angrily, "How can a woman be dragged a thousand li to be mixed among male officials and soldiers—this is a gross violation of propriety!

sentences.zh: 自今毋得逮婦人。」

translations.literal: From now on women must not be arrested."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth women must not be arrested."

sentences.zh: 建議著為令。

translations.literal: He memorialized that this be instituted as law.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that this provision be enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢湖南道廉訪使，調海道都漕運萬戶。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Vice Censor of the Hunan Circuit and transferred to Wanhu of the Maritime Grand Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Vice Censor of the Hunan Circuit and transferred to Wanhu of the Maritime Grand Grain Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 是歲，當天歷之變，海漕舟有後至直沽者，不果輸，复漕而南還，行省欲坐罪督運者，勒其還趨直沽。

translations.literal: That year, at the time of the Tianli succession crisis, sea-transport ships that arrived late at Zhigu could not deliver their cargo and had to sail south again; the Branch Secretariat wished to punish the transport supervisors and compelled them to return to Zhigu.
translations.idiomatic: That year, during the Tianli succession crisis, sea-transport ships that arrived late at Zhigu could not unload their cargo and had to sail south again; the Branch Secretariat wished to punish the transport supervisors and ordered them back to Zhigu.

sentences.zh: 克敬以謂：「脫其常年而往返若是，信可罪。

translations.literal: Kejing said, "If in normal years they traveled back and forth like this, they could indeed be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "If in ordinary years they had traveled back and forth in this fashion, they could indeed be punished.

sentences.zh: 今蹈萬死，完所漕而還，豈得已哉！」

translations.literal: Now having braved ten thousand perils and completed their transport before returning, how could they have done otherwise!"
translations.idiomatic: But having braved deadly perils and completed their transport before returning, how could they have done otherwise!"

sentences.zh: 乃請令其計石數，附次年所漕舟達京師，省臣從之。

translations.literal: He then petitioned to have them count the shi of grain and attach it to the following year's transport ships to reach the capital; the provincial officials agreed.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned that they count the grain by shi and have it delivered to the capital on the following year's transport ships; the provincial authorities agreed.

sentences.zh: 召為參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Councilor of Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Councilor of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 有以飛語中大臣者，下其事，克敬持古八議之法，謂勳貴可以不議，且罪狀不明而輕罪大臣，何以白天下。

translations.literal: Someone used rumor to strike at a high minister; the matter was referred down; Kejing upheld the ancient Eight Deliberations law, saying meritorious nobles need not be deliberated upon, and that with charges unclear to lightly punish a great minister—how could this be explained to the world.
translations.idiomatic: Someone used slander to attack a high minister; when the case was referred down, Kejing invoked the ancient law of the Eight Deliberations, arguing that meritorious nobles were exempt from such proceedings, and that to punish a great minister lightly when the charges were unclear—how could this be justified to the world.

sentences.zh: 宰相傳旨大長公主為皇外姑，賜錢若干；

translations.literal: The chancellor transmitted an order that the Grand Princess, as the emperor's maternal aunt, was to be granted a certain sum of money;
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor transmitted orders that the Grand Princess, as the emperor's maternal aunt, was to receive a grant of money;

sentences.zh: 平雲南軍還，賜錢若干；

translations.literal: the army returning from pacifying Yunnan was to be granted a certain sum of money;
translations.idiomatic: the army returning from pacifying Yunnan was to receive a grant of money;

sentences.zh: 英后入覲，賜錢若干。

translations.literal: and the Empress, on entering the capital to pay homage, was to be granted a certain sum of money.
translations.idiomatic: and the Empress, upon entering the capital to pay homage, was to receive a grant of money.

sentences.zh: 克敬乞覆奏，宰相怒曰：「參議乃敢格詔命邪！」

translations.literal: Kejing requested reconsideration; the chancellor angrily said, "A Councilor dares obstruct imperial commands!"
translations.idiomatic: Kejing requested that the orders be reported back for reconsideration; the chancellor said angrily, "How dare a Councilor obstruct imperial commands!"

sentences.zh: 克敬曰：「用財宜有道，大長公主供饋素優，今賜錢出無名，不當也。

translations.literal: Kejing said, "The use of wealth should follow principle; the Grand Princess's provisions are already ample—now to grant money without cause is improper.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "Public funds should be spent with good reason; the Grand Princess already enjoys ample provisions—granting money without cause is improper.

sentences.zh: 自諸軍征討以來，賞格未下，平雲南省獨先受賞，是不均也。

translations.literal: Since the various armies began their campaigns, reward schedules have not yet been issued, yet the Yunnan pacification force alone receives rewards first—this is inequitable.
translations.idiomatic: Since the various armies began their campaigns, reward schedules have not yet been issued, yet the Yunnan pacification force alone is rewarded first—this is inequitable.

sentences.zh: 英後遠還，徒禦眾多，非大錫賚，恩意不能洽，今賜物鮮少，是不周也。」

translations.literal: The Empress returns from afar with many attendants; without a great grant her favor cannot be fully shown—yet the gifts now granted are few—this is not thorough."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress returns from afar with many attendants; without a generous grant her favor cannot be fully shown—yet the gifts granted are meager—this is inadequate."

sentences.zh: 宰相以聞，帝可其議。

translations.literal: The chancellor reported upward, and the emperor approved his reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor reported to the throne, and the emperor approved his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 拜中奉大夫、參知政事，行省遼陽。

translations.literal: He was appointed Central Submitter Grand Master and Vice Administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Central Submitter Grand Master and Vice Administrator of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄除江南行台治書侍御史，又遷淮東廉訪使，以正綱紀為己任，不縱貪墨，不阿宗戚，聲譽益著。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Secretariat Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, then transferred to Vice Censor of the Huaidong Circuit; he took rectifying discipline as his duty, did not indulge the greedy and corrupt, did not curry favor with imperial clansmen, and his reputation grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Secretariat Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, then transferred to Vice Censor of the Huaidong Circuit; he made rectifying discipline his duty, refused to indulge corruption, would not curry favor with imperial clansmen, and his reputation grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書，乘傳至淮安，墜馬，居吳中養疾。

translations.literal: He entered office as Minister of Personnel; while traveling by relay post to Huai'an he fell from his horse and remained in Wu to recover from illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Personnel; while traveling by relay post to Huai'an he fell from his horse and remained in Wu to recover from illness.

sentences.zh: 元統初，起為江浙行省參知政事，請罷富民承佃江淮田，從之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuantong he was recalled as Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and requested abolition of wealthy households' contracting of Jiang-Huai fields; his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuantong reign he was recalled as Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and petitioned to abolish the practice of wealthy households contracting Jiang-Huai fields; his petition was granted.

sentences.zh: 松江大姓，有歲漕米萬石獻京師者，其人既死，子孫貧且行乞，有司仍歲徵，弗足則雜置松江田賦中，令民包納。

translations.literal: In Songjiang a great clan annually presented ten thousand shi of transport grain to the capital; after the man died his descendants were poor and even begged, yet the authorities still levied it yearly, and when insufficient mixed it into Songjiang land tax for the people to pay in lump sum.
translations.idiomatic: In Songjiang a great clan had annually presented ten thousand shi of transport grain to the capital; after the donor died his descendants were poor and even begged, yet the authorities still levied it yearly, and when the amount fell short they folded it into Songjiang land tax for the people to pay collectively.

sentences.zh: 克敬曰：「匹夫妄獻米，徼名爵以榮一身，今身死家破，又已奪其爵，不可使一郡之人均受其害，國用寧乏此耶！」

translations.literal: Kejing said, "A commoner rashly presented grain to win a title and honor himself alone; now his person is dead and family ruined, and his rank has already been taken away—one cannot let an entire commandery suffer for this; would state revenue lack this amount!"
translations.idiomatic: Kejing said, "A commoner rashly presented grain to win an honor for himself alone; now he is dead, his family ruined, and his rank already revoked—we cannot let an entire commandery suffer for this; will state revenue truly lack this amount!"

sentences.zh: 具論免之。

translations.literal: He fully argued for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in full for exemption.

sentences.zh: 江浙大旱，諸民田減租，唯長寧寺田不減，遂移牘中書，以謂不可忽天變而毒疲民。

translations.literal: Jiang-Zhe suffered great drought; the people's fields had rent reduced, but Changning Temple fields alone were not reduced; he therefore sent a document to the Central Secretariat saying one must not ignore heaven's warnings and harm the exhausted people.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe suffered severe drought; rent was reduced on commoners' fields, but Changning Temple fields alone were not reduced; he sent a memorial to the Central Secretariat arguing that one must not ignore heaven's warnings and harm the exhausted populace.

sentences.zh: 嶺海徭賊竊發，朝廷調戍兵之在行省者往討之，會提調軍馬官缺，故事，漢人不得與軍政，眾莫知所為，克敬抗言：「行省任方面之寄，假令萬一有重於此者，亦將拘法坐視邪！」

translations.literal: Yao bandits in Linghai stole out in rebellion; the court mobilized garrison troops in the Branch Secretariat to suppress them; when the post for coordinating military horses was vacant, by precedent Han Chinese could not hold military administration, and none knew what to do; Kejing boldly said, "The Branch Secretariat bears responsibility for a whole region—suppose there were something weightier than this—would one still sit bound by law and look on!"
translations.idiomatic: Yao bandits in Linghai rose in rebellion; the court mobilized garrison troops of the Branch Secretariat to suppress them; when the post for coordinating military horses fell vacant, precedent held that Han Chinese could not hold military posts, and no one knew what to do; Kejing declared boldly, "The Branch Secretariat bears responsibility for an entire region—if something even graver than this arose, would we still sit bound by law and do nothing!"

sentences.zh: 乃調兵往捕之，軍行給糧有差。

translations.literal: He then mobilized troops to capture them, and grain rations on campaign were graded by rank.
translations.idiomatic: He then mobilized troops to capture them, with graded grain rations for troops on campaign.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，即令江西、湖廣二省給糧亦如之。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported to court, the court at once ordered Jiangxi and Huguang provinces likewise to supply grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the court immediately ordered Jiangxi and Huguang provinces likewise to supply grain.

sentences.zh: 視事五月，請老，年甫五十九。

translations.literal: After five months in office he requested retirement, being only fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After five months in office he requested retirement, though he was only fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 謂人曰：「​​穴趾而峻墉，必危；

translations.literal: He told others, "To dig out the toes and raise the wall high must bring danger;
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "To dig away the toes and raise the wall high must bring danger;

sentences.zh: 再實之木，必傷其根。

translations.literal: a tree that bears fruit twice must injure its roots.
translations.idiomatic: a tree that bears fruit twice must injure its roots.

sentences.zh: 無功德而忝富貴，何以異此？

translations.literal: Without merit or virtue yet enjoying wealth and rank—how does this differ from that?
translations.idiomatic: To enjoy wealth and rank without merit or virtue—how is this different?

sentences.zh: 故常懷止足之分也。」

translations.literal: Therefore I always keep in mind the boundary of knowing when to stop."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I always keep in mind the boundary of knowing when to stop."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「世俗喜言勿認真，此非名言。

translations.literal: He also said, "The world likes to say 'do not be too serious'—this is not a fine saying.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "People like to say 'do not take things too seriously'—this is not wise counsel.

sentences.zh: 臨事不認真，豈盡忠之道乎？」

translations.literal: If in handling affairs one is not serious, how is that the way of full loyalty?"
translations.idiomatic: If in handling affairs one is not serious, how can that be the way of full loyalty?"

sentences.zh: 故其歷官所至，俱有政績可紀，時稱名卿。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever he held office there were achievements worth recording, and his age called him a renowned minister."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore wherever he held office he left achievements worth recording, and his contemporaries called him a renowned minister."

sentences.zh: 克敬喜讀書，其有所得者，輒抄為書。

translations.literal: Kejing delighted in reading; whatever he gained he would copy into books.
translations.idiomatic: Kejing loved reading; whatever insights he gained he copied into books.

sentences.zh: 又有所著詩文奏議傳於世。

translations.literal: He also had literary works, memorials, and deliberations transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also left literary works, memorials, and policy papers that circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 元統三年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuantong he died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Yuantong reign (1335), at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈中奉大夫、陝西等處行省參知政事，追封梁郡公，諡文肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Central Submitter Grand Master and Vice Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, with posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Central Submitter Grand Master and Vice Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Liang, with the posthumous epithet Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子時，以文學顯，歷仕中書參知政事，至左丞，以翰林學士承旨致仕。

translations.literal: His son Shi, distinguished in letters, served successively as Vice Administrator of the Central Secretariat, then Left Chancellor, and retired as Hanlin Academician Exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi, distinguished in letters, rose to Vice Administrator of the Central Secretariat, then Left Chancellor, and retired as Hanlin Academician Exemplar.

sentences.zh: ○任速哥

translations.literal: ○ Ren Suge
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ren Suge

sentences.zh: 任速哥，渤海人。

translations.literal: Ren Suge was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Suge was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 自幼事父母以孝稱。

translations.literal: From youth he served his parents and was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he served his parents and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻，尤峭直，疏財而尚氣，不尚勢利。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and unconstrained, especially stern and upright, generous with wealth and valuing spirit, not esteeming power and profit.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and unconventional, especially stern and upright, generous with wealth and valuing honor, and disdainful of power and profit.

sentences.zh: 義之所在，必亟為之，有古俠士風。

translations.literal: Where righteousness lay he would surely act quickly, having the air of ancient knights-errant.
translations.idiomatic: Where righteousness lay he acted at once, displaying the spirit of the knights-errant of old.

sentences.zh: 而家居恂恂，儒者不能過。

translations.literal: Yet at home he was respectful and cautious, which Confucians could not surpass.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at home he was respectful and cautious beyond what most Confucians could match.

sentences.zh: 初襲父官，為右衛千戶。

translations.literal: Initially he inherited his father's office as chiliarch of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He first inherited his father's post as chiliarch of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 公卿以其賢，薦於朝。

translations.literal: Dukes and ministers, because he was worthy, recommended him to court.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and ministers, recognizing his worth, recommended him to court.

sentences.zh: 英宗召見，與語奇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yingzong summoned him for an audience and, conversing with him, found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong summoned him for an audience and, in conversation, found him remarkable.

sentences.zh: 由是出入禁闥，待以心腹，將擇重職處之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he moved in and out of the forbidden precincts and was treated as a trusted confidant; the court was about to choose a weighty post for him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he moved in and out of the forbidden precincts and was treated as a trusted confidant; the court was about to place him in a weighty post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，鐵失與倒剌沙構謀，英宗遇弒，遂引去。

translations.literal: Before long, Tieshi and Daula Shah plotted together; Emperor Yingzong was assassinated, and Suge then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tieshi and Daula Shah plotted together; Emperor Yingzong was assassinated, and Suge then withdrew from office.

sentences.zh: 自是不復出仕，居常扼腕，或醉歸，慟哭過市，時人目以為狂，莫知其意也。

translations.literal: From then on he never again took office; he often clenched his fist in grief, and sometimes when drunk returning home would wail passing through the market; people of the time regarded him as mad and did not know his intent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he never served again; he often clenched his fists in grief, and sometimes when drunk would wail as he passed through the market; people regarded him as mad and did not understand his purpose.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，倒剌沙用事，天變數見。

translations.literal: In the Taiding reign Daula Shah held power, and heaven's warnings appeared repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding reign Daula Shah held power, and heaven's warnings appeared repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 速哥乃密與平章政事速速謀曰：「先帝之仇，孤臣朝夕痛心而不能報者，以未有善策也。

translations.literal: Suge then secretly said to Vice Administrator Susu, "The former emperor's enemy—as a lone subject I grieve day and night yet cannot repay, for I have had no good plan.
translations.idiomatic: Suge then said secretly to Vice Administrator Susu, "The former emperor's enemy—as a lone subject I grieve day and night yet cannot repay him, for I have had no good plan.

sentences.zh: 今吾思之，武宗有子二人，長子周王，正統所屬，然遠居朔方，難以達意。

translations.literal: Now I have thought: Emperor Wuzong had two sons; the eldest, the Prince of Zhou, belongs to the legitimate succession, yet he dwells far in the northern frontier and is hard to reach with our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have considered: Emperor Wuzong had two sons; the eldest, the Prince of Zhou, holds the legitimate succession, yet he dwells far on the northern frontier and is hard to reach with our intent.

sentences.zh: 次子懷王，人望所歸，而近在金陵，易於傳命。

translations.literal: The second son, the Prince of Huai, is where popular regard gathers, and he is near at Jinling, easy to convey orders to.
translations.idiomatic: The second son, the Prince of Huai, commands popular regard and is nearby at Jinling, where orders are easy to convey.

sentences.zh: 若能同心推戴，以圖大計，則先帝之仇可雪也。」

translations.literal: If we can with one heart support and enthrone him to plan the great undertaking, then the former emperor's enemy can be avenged."
translations.idiomatic: If we can unite in supporting and enthroning him to carry out the great plan, the former emperor's enemy can be avenged."

sentences.zh: 速速深然之。

translations.literal: Susu deeply agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Susu deeply agreed.

sentences.zh: 時燕帖木兒方僉樞密院事，實握兵柄，二人深結納之。

translations.literal: At that time El Temür was concurrently Vice Minister of the Bureau of Military Affairs and in fact held military power; the two men deeply befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time El Temür held concurrent office in the Bureau of Military Affairs and in fact controlled military power; the two men cultivated a deep bond with him.

sentences.zh: 冬，乃告以所謀，燕帖木兒初聞之矍然。

translations.literal: In winter they told him of the plan; El Temür at first hearing started in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they revealed the plan to him; El Temür at first started in alarm.

sentences.zh: 因徐說之曰：「天下之事，惟順逆兩途，以順討逆，何患不克。

translations.literal: He then slowly persuaded him, saying, "Affairs under heaven have only two paths, compliance and defiance; to use compliance to attack defiance, what worry is there of not succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: He then slowly persuaded him, saying, "Affairs under heaven have only two paths, compliance and defiance; to use the compliant to attack the defiant, what fear is there of failure.

sentences.zh: 況公國家世臣，與國同休戚，今國難不恤，他日有先我而謀者，禍必及矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover you are a hereditary minister of the state, sharing weal and woe with the realm; now if national difficulty is not relieved, another day someone may act before us and disaster will reach us as well."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover you are a hereditary minister of the state, sharing weal and woe with the realm; if national crisis is not addressed now, another day someone may act before us and disaster will reach us too."

sentences.zh: 於是燕帖木兒許之。

translations.literal: Thereupon El Temür agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon El Temür agreed.

sentences.zh: 致和元年，懷王自金陵遷江陵，俄而泰定帝崩，倒剌沙踰月不立君，物情洶洶，速哥乃與速速從燕帖木兒奉豫王令，率諸豪傑，乘時奮義，以八月四日執居守省臣，發兵塞居庸諸關，召文武百僚集闕下，諭以翊戴大義，遣使迎懷王於江陵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhihe the Prince of Huai moved from Jinling to Jiangling; soon Emperor Taiding died, and Daula Shah for more than a month did not enthrone a ruler; popular feeling was turbulent; Suge then with Susu, following El Temür under the Prince of Yu's order, led the heroes of the age to seize the moment and rise in righteousness; on the fourth day of the eighth month they seized the provincial officials holding the capital, sent troops to block the Juyong passes, summoned the civil and military officials below the palace gate, explained the great principle of supporting enthronement, and dispatched envoys to welcome the Prince of Huai from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhihe the Prince of Huai moved from Jinling to Jiangling; soon Emperor Taiding died, and Daula Shah for more than a month enthroned no ruler; popular feeling grew turbulent; Suge then with Susu, following El Temür under the Prince of Yu's order, led the heroes of the age to seize the moment and rise in righteousness; on the fourth day of the eighth month they seized the provincial officials holding the capital, sent troops to block the Juyong passes, summoned civil and military officials below the palace gate, explained the great principle of enthronement, and dispatched envoys to welcome the Prince of Huai from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 懷王至京師，群臣請正大統，遂即皇帝位，是為文宗。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Huai reached the capital the officials requested correction of the great succession, and he then ascended the imperial throne—this was Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Huai reached the capital the officials requested that the great succession be set right, and he ascended the throne—this was Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 論功行賞，擢速哥為禮部尚書，速哥辭曰：「臣曩備宿衛，南坡之變，不能勇效一死，以報國士之知。

translations.literal: When merits were assessed and rewards given, Suge was promoted to Minister of Rites; Suge declined, saying, "I formerly served in the night guard; at the Nanpo incident I could not bravely offer my death in one act to repay the state warrior's knowledge of me.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were assessed and rewards distributed, Suge was promoted to Minister of Rites; Suge declined, saying, "I formerly served in the night guard; at the Nanpo incident I could not bravely die in one stroke to repay what the state warrior knew of me.

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，皆諸將相之力，在臣未足贖罪，又曷敢言功乎！」

translations.literal: Today's achievement is all the strength of the generals and ministers; in me it is not enough to redeem guilt—how dare I speak of merit!"
translations.idiomatic: Today's achievement rests on the generals and ministers; for me it is not enough to redeem guilt—how dare I speak of merit!"

sentences.zh: 文宗慰勉之，乃拜命。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong comforted and encouraged him, and he then accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong comforted and encouraged him, and he then accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 而其他賞賚，一無所受。

translations.literal: But other rewards and gifts he accepted not one.
translations.idiomatic: But other rewards and gifts he accepted not a single one.

sentences.zh: 尋遷長寧寺卿，繼出為安豐路總管，又入為壽福府總管，又為都水使者，居官恂恂，無幾微自伐之意。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of Changning Temple, then went out as General Administrator of Anfeng Circuit, then entered as Director of the Shoufu Office, then became Commissioner of Waterworks; in office he was respectful and cautious, without the slightest air of self-praise.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Director of Changning Temple, then posted out as General Administrator of Anfeng Circuit, then recalled as Director of the Shoufu Office, then appointed Commissioner of Waterworks; in office he was respectful and cautious, without the slightest hint of self-congratulation.

sentences.zh: 人或詢以翊戴之事，往往遜謝，終無所言，君子尤以是多之。

translations.literal: When people inquired about the enthronement affair he often declined with humility and in the end said nothing; gentlemen especially for this praised him more.
translations.idiomatic: When people inquired about the enthronement affair he often demurred and in the end said nothing; men of discernment especially admired him for this.

sentences.zh: ○陳思謙

translations.literal: ○ Chen Siqian
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chen Siqian

sentences.zh: 陳思謙，字景讓，其家世見祖祐傳中。

translations.literal: Chen Siqian, styled Jingrang—his family history is seen in the biography of his ancestor You.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Siqian, styled Jingrang—his family history appears in the biography of his ancestor You.

sentences.zh: 思謙少孤，警敏好學，凡名物度數、綱紀本末，考訂詳究，尤深於邵子《皇極經世書》。

translations.literal: Siqian was orphaned young, alert and clever and fond of learning; in all names and things, measures and numbers, the essentials of institutions from root to branch, he examined and determined in detail, especially deeply in Shao Yong's Huangji Jingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian lost his father young; alert and clever, he loved learning; in all names and things, measures and numbers, and the essentials of institutions from root to branch, he investigated with meticulous care, especially mastering Shao Yong's Huangji Jingshi.

sentences.zh: 文宗天歷初政，收攬賢能，丞相高昌王亦都護舉思謙，時年四十矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Wenzong's Tianli administration he gathered the worthy and able; Chancellor Yiduhu of Gaochang recommended Siqian when he was already forty.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Wenzong's Tianli administration the court gathered worthy men; Chancellor Yidu Hu of Gaochang recommended Siqian when he was already forty.

sentences.zh: 召見興聖宮。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience at the Xingsheng Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned for audience at the Xingsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，授典寶監經歷。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he was appointed Manager of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was appointed Manager of the Directorate of Imperial Treasures.

sentences.zh: 十一月，改禮部主事，首言：「教坊、儀鳳二司，請併入宣徽，以清禮部之選。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he was changed to Clerk of the Ministry of Rites and spoke first, saying, "The two offices of the Music Bureau and the Ceremonial Phoenix Office should be merged into the Imperial Entertainment Commission to clarify the Ministry of Rites's selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was transferred to Clerk of the Ministry of Rites and spoke first, saying, "The Music Bureau and the Ceremonial Phoenix Office should be merged into the Imperial Entertainment Commission to clarify the Ministry of Rites's selections.

sentences.zh: 其官屬不當與文武臣並列朝會，宜置百官之後、大樂之前。」

translations.literal: Their officials should not stand in court assemblies together with civil and military ministers; they should be placed after the hundred officials and before the great music."
translations.idiomatic: Their personnel should not stand together with civil and military ministers at court assemblies; they should be placed after the hundred officials and before the great music."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved this.

sentences.zh: 而二司隸禮部如故。

translations.literal: Yet the two offices remained subordinate to the Ministry of Rites as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two offices remained subordinate to the Ministry of Rites as before.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，拜西行台監察御史，建明八事：一曰正君道，二曰結人心，三曰崇禮讓，四曰正綱紀，五曰審銓衡，六曰勵孝行，七曰紓民力，八曰修軍政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Western Branch Censorate and set forth eight matters: first, rectify the ruler's Way; second, bind people's hearts; third, honor ritual and deference; fourth, rectify institutions; fifth, examine selection; sixth, encourage filial conduct; seventh, relieve the people's strength; eighth, repair military administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhishun he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Western Branch Censorate and set forth eight proposals: first, rectify the ruler's Way; second, bind the people's hearts; third, honor ritual and deference; fourth, rectify institutions; fifth, examine civil-service selection; sixth, encourage filial conduct; seventh, relieve the people's burdens; eighth, repair military administration.

sentences.zh: 先是，關陝大饑，民多鬻產流徙，及來歸，皆無地可耕，思謙言：「聽民倍直贖之，使富者收兼入之利，貧者獲已棄之業。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Guan-Shaan suffered great famine; many people sold property and wandered away; when they returned all had no land to till; Siqian said, "Let the people redeem at double price, so the rich receive the profit of combined entry and the poor regain abandoned livelihood."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Guan-Shaan had suffered severe famine; many people sold their property and wandered away; when they returned they had no land to till; Siqian proposed, "Let the people redeem their land at double the sale price, so the rich receive fair profit and the poor regain their abandoned livelihood."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 監察御史李擴行部甘肅，金州民劉海延都，其男元元，自稱流民王延祿，非海延都之子，告海延都掠其財。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Li Kuo toured Gansu; a Jinzhou commoner Liu Haiyandu had a son Yuanyuan who called himself the refugee Wang Yanlu, not Haiyandu's son, and accused Haiyandu of seizing his property.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Li Kuo toured Gansu; a Jinzhou commoner named Liu Haiyandu had a son Yuanyuan who claimed to be the refugee Wang Yanlu, not Haiyandu's son, and accused Haiyandu of seizing his property.

sentences.zh: 擴聽之，以酷法抑其父。

translations.literal: Kuo listened to him and used harsh law to suppress the father.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo believed him and used harsh law to suppress the father.

sentences.zh: 思謙劾擴逆父子之天，壞朝廷之法，遂抵擴罪。

translations.literal: Siqian impeached Kuo for violating the heaven of father and son and ruining the court's law, and Kuo was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Siqian impeached Kuo for violating the natural bond of father and son and undermining the court's law, and Kuo was punished.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，遷太禧宗禋院都事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Ancestral Sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Ancestral Sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 九月，拜監察御史，首陳四事，言：「上有宗廟社稷之重，下有四海烝民之生，前有祖宗垂創之艱，後有子孫長久之計。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Investigating Censor and first set forth four matters, saying, "Above there is the weight of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain; below there is the life of the myriad people under heaven; before there is the hardship of the ancestors' founding enterprise; behind there is the long-term plan for sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Investigating Censor and first set forth four matters, saying, "Above lies the weight of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain; below lies the life of the myriad people; before lies the hardship of the ancestors' founding enterprise; behind lies the long-term plan for sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 中論秦、漢以來，上下三千餘年，天直一統者，六百餘年而已。

translations.literal: In the middle he discussed from Qin and Han down more than three thousand years; heaven's direct unity lasted only a little more than six hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Between them he observed that from Qin and Han down through more than three thousand years, periods of direct unity under heaven totaled only a little more than six hundred years.

sentences.zh: 我朝開國，百有餘年，混一六十餘年，土宇人民，三代、漢、唐所未有也。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's founding has been a little more than a hundred years, unified more than sixty years; territory and people are what the Three Dynasties, Han, and Tang never had.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has ruled for more than a hundred years and been unified for more than sixty; in territory and population it surpasses the Three Dynasties, Han, and Tang.

sentences.zh: 民有千金之產，猶謹守之，以為先人所營，況君臨天下，承祖宗艱難之業，而傳祚萬世者乎！

translations.literal: A commoner with a thousand-cash estate still guards it carefully as what ancestors built—how much more for one who rules all under heaven, inherits the ancestors' difficult enterprise, and transmits the throne for ten thousand generations!
translations.idiomatic: A commoner with a thousand-cash estate still guards it carefully as what his ancestors built—how much more for one who rules all under heaven, inherits the ancestors' arduous enterprise, and transmits the throne for ten thousand generations!

sentences.zh: 臣愚以興亡懇懇言者，誠以皇上有元之聖主，今日乃皇上盛時圖治之機，茲不可失也。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly speaks earnestly of rise and fall because truly Your Majesty has a sage ruler of the Yuan, and today is the emperor's flourishing time and the opportunity to seek good governance—this must not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant speaks earnestly of rise and fall because Your Majesty is a sage ruler of the Yuan, and today is the emperor's flourishing age and the opportunity to seek good governance—this must not be lost."

sentences.zh: 又言：「戶部賜田，諸怯薛支請，海青獅豹肉食，及局院工糧，好事布施，一切泛支，以至元三十年以前較之，動增數十倍。

translations.literal: He also said, "Ministry of Revenue grant fields, various keshig requests, sea-eagle and lion and leopard meat rations, bureau and office craftsmen grain, charitable donations, and all miscellaneous expenditures—compared with before the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan they generally increased several tens of times.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Grant fields from the Ministry of Revenue, various keshig requests, rations of meat for hunting birds and lions and leopards, craftsmen's grain for bureaus and offices, charitable donations, and all miscellaneous expenditures—compared with the period before the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan they have generally increased several tens of times.

sentences.zh: 至順經費，缺二百三十九萬餘錠。

translations.literal: Zhishun expenditures were short by more than 2,390,000 ding of paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhishun expenditures fell short by more than 2,390,000 ding of paper notes.

sentences.zh: 宜節無益不急之費，以備軍國之用，苟能三分損一以惠民，夫豈小哉！」

translations.literal: One should cut useless and non-urgent expenses to prepare for military and state use; if one could reduce by a third to benefit the people, would that not be great!"
translations.idiomatic: One should cut useless and non-urgent expenses to prepare for military and state needs; if one could reduce expenditures by a third to benefit the people, would that not be a great gain!"

sentences.zh: 又言：「軍站消乏，簽補則無殷實之戶，接濟則無羨餘之財，倘有徵行，必括民間之馬，苟能修馬政，亦其一助也。

translations.literal: He also said, "Military relay stations are depleted; when registering replacements there are no wealthy households, when providing relief there is no surplus wealth; if there is a campaign one must conscript the people's horses; if horse administration can be repaired, that too is one aid.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Military relay stations are depleted; when registering replacements there are no wealthy households, when providing relief there is no surplus funds; if a campaign arises the people's horses must be conscripted; if horse administration can be restored, that too would help.

sentences.zh: 方今西越流沙，北際沙漠，東及遼海，地氣高寒，水甘草美，無非牧養之地，宜設置群牧使司，統領十監，專治馬政，並畜牛羊，數年之後，馬實蕃盛，或給軍以收兵威，或給站以優民力，牛羊之富，又足以給國用，非小補也。」

translations.literal: Now in the west beyond the drifting sands, north to the desert, east to the Liao sea—the climate is high and cold, water and grass fine—there is nowhere that is not pasture land; one should establish a Directorate of Herds to oversee ten superintendencies, specialize in horse administration, and also raise cattle and sheep; after several years horses will truly flourish, either supplied to the army to gather military might or supplied to stations to ease the people's strength; the wealth of cattle and sheep would also suffice for state use—not a small supplement."
translations.idiomatic: Today from the western deserts beyond the drifting sands, north to the desert, east to the Liao sea—the land is high and cold, the water and grass excellent—almost nowhere is unsuited to pasturage; a Directorate of Herds should be established to oversee ten superintendencies, specialize in horse administration, and also raise cattle and sheep; after several years horses would flourish abundantly, supplied either to the army to strengthen military power or to relay stations to ease the people's burdens; the wealth of cattle and sheep would also suffice for state use—a substantial benefit."

sentences.zh: 又言：「銓衡之弊，入仕之門太多，黜陟之法太簡，州郡之任太淹，朝省之除太速，欲設三策，以救四弊。

translations.literal: He also said, "The abuses of selection: doors into office are too many, methods of demotion and promotion too simple, prefectural and commandery posts too long in tenure, metropolitan appointments too swift—wishing to set three policies to remedy four abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The abuses of civil-service selection: too many paths into office, demotion and promotion too simplistic, prefectural posts held too long, metropolitan appointments made too swiftly—I propose three policies to remedy four abuses.

sentences.zh: 一曰，至元三十年以後增設衙門，冗濫不急者，從實減並，其外有選法者，併入中書。

translations.literal: First, yamens added after the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan that are redundant and not urgent should be reduced and merged according to fact; those outside with selection methods should be merged into the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: First, government offices added after the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan that are redundant and non-essential should be reduced and merged as warranted; those with selection procedures should be consolidated under the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二曰，宜參酌古制，設辟舉之科，令三品以下，各舉所知，得才則受賞，失實則受罰。
